q: What does BBPS stand for?
explain: BBPS is the Bharat Bill Payment System, an interoperable bill payment ecosystem driven by NPCI.

q: Which of the following is a standard format of Bank Identifier Codes (BIC) used to identify banks and financial institutions globally?
explain: SWIFT codes, also called BIC, identify banks worldwide. IFSC works only for domestic transfers.

q: Which of the following is a benefit associated with RuPay?
options: Processing fees are considerably lower than for regular debit or credit cards
explain: RuPay processes transactions domestically, which lowers costs and processing fees compared with international card networks.

q: Which of the following is NOT a product of NPCI?
explain: SEPA is a European payment scheme. UPI, BHIM and BBPS are all NPCI products.

q: Which card is a new card payment scheme launched by NPCI?
explain: RuPay is the domestic card scheme conceived and launched by NPCI on 26 March 2012.

q: In the abbreviation UPI, what does the letter 'I' stand for?
explain: UPI is the Unified Payments Interface.

q: IMPS, the instant inter-bank fund transfer service through mobile phones, stands for which of the following?
explain: IMPS is the Immediate Payment Service, available 24x7 including bank holidays.

q: Which agency developed the Unified Payments Interface?
options: Department of Electronics and Information Technology
explain: UPI was developed by NPCI, which runs India's retail payment systems.

q: Which statement about BBPS is correct?
options: SEBI drives it and it runs only on working days
RBI conceptualised it and NPCI drives it, offering interoperable bill payment
explain: BBPS is an RBI-conceptualised system driven by NPCI, covering many bill categories and payment modes.

q: Which of the following is NOT required for a customer to transact through AePS?
options: Issuer Identification Number of the bank
explain: AePS relies on Aadhaar number, biometric authentication and the bank's identification number, so no card PIN is needed.

q: The open platform launched by NPCI for instant mobile-based bank-to-bank transfers is called what?
explain: It is the Unified Payments Interface (UPI).

q: Which of the following is NOT a benefit of RuPay?
options: Users cannot get alerts for each transaction
explain: RuPay users do get alerts for every transaction. The other three are genuine benefits.

q: The Aadhaar Enabled Payment System (AePS) enables banking through business correspondents. Which of these is NOT among its basic Aadhaar-enabled transactions?
explain: AePS covers balance enquiry, cash deposit, cash withdrawal and Aadhaar-to-Aadhaar transfer, but not overdrafts.

q: NPCI is the umbrella organisation for which type of payments in India?
explain: NPCI is the umbrella organisation for all retail payment and settlement systems in India.

q: Under which Act was NPCI set up to create payment and settlement infrastructure?
explain: NPCI was set up under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007 with RBI and IBA guidance.

q: NPCI was incorporated as a 'Not for Profit' company under Section 25 of the Companies Act 1956. Which section of the Companies Act 2013 corresponds to it?
explain: Section 25 of the 1956 Act is now Section 8 of the Companies Act 2013.

q: Which of the following is NOT one of NPCI's promoter banks?
explain: The ten promoter banks are SBI, PNB, Canara, Bank of Baroda, Union Bank, Bank of India, ICICI, HDFC, Citibank and HSBC.

q: How many promoter banks does NPCI have as per the book?
explain: There are 10 promoter banks: six public, two private and two foreign.

q: The Aadhaar Payment Bridge System (APBS) is mainly used for what?
options: Transferring DBT benefits and subsidies using Aadhaar numbers
explain: Government departments use APBS to transfer subsidies and benefits under Direct Benefit Transfer schemes.

q: AePS allows basic banking transactions using Aadhaar authentication at which point?
options: A Micro ATM through a business correspondent
explain: AePS works through Micro ATMs run by business correspondents of any bank.

q: On which date was BBPS launched by NPCI?
explain: BBPS was launched on 31 August 2016. 30 December 2016 is the BHIM launch date.

q: BBPS was launched on the recommendation of a committee headed by which RBI Executive Director?
explain: The G. Padmanabhan Committee recommended BBPS.

q: BBPS services are available on which schedule?
explain: BBPS runs round the clock on all days, including public holidays.

q: In which country is SWIFT based?
explain: SWIFT is a Belgium-based secure financial messaging service.

q: SWIFT became operational in which year and month?
explain: SWIFT became operational in May 1977.

q: SWIFT is best described as which of the following?
explain: SWIFT is a bank-owned, non-profit cooperative society serving over 11,000 institutions in 200+ countries.

q: The RTGS system was opened in India on which date?
explain: RTGS opened in India on 29 April 2004; NEFT followed in November 2005.

q: When was NEFT introduced in India?
explain: NEFT was introduced in November 2005.

q: From which date has RTGS been available 24x7x365?
explain: RTGS became 24x7x365 from 4 December 2020. NEFT became 24x7 in December 2019.

q: What limit applies to the amount that can be transferred through NEFT?
explain: NEFT has neither a minimum nor a maximum limit on the amount.

q: Fund transfer via NEFT initiated online through internet or mobile banking is treated how?
explain: Online NEFT is free; only transfers via a bank branch carry a charge of up to ₹25 plus taxes.

q: What is the USSD code used to access NPCI's National Unified USSD Platform?
explain: The NUUP is accessed by dialling *99# on any phone, basic or smart.

q: When was the USSD-based National Unified USSD Platform (*99#) first launched?
explain: The service was initially launched in November 2012.

q: In the 11-character IFSC, what do the last six characters denote?
explain: The first four characters identify the bank and the last six identify the branch.

q: What is ECS-Debit used for?
options: Collecting utility charges, premiums and loan instalments from customer accounts
explain: ECS-Debit pulls recurring dues from many accounts. ECS-Credit is for paying interest or dividends to many beneficiaries.

q: UPI Autopay, which enables recurring e-mandates, was launched by NPCI in which month and year?
explain: UPI Autopay was launched in August 2020 for recurring payments such as EMIs and subscriptions.

q: Which of the following is NOT a way to send money on UPI?
explain: UPI uses VPA, mobile number, account number with IFSC, Aadhaar and QR code. Cheque numbers are not used.

q: Which statement about UPI is correct?
options: One app can link only one account
UPI works only on working days
Multiple bank accounts can be linked to a single UPI app
UPI works only on feature phones
explain: Any UPI client app can be used and several bank accounts can be linked to one app.

q: Bharat QR was launched in which month and year?
explain: Bharat QR was launched in September 2016 to help India become a less-cash society.

q: What is the advantage of dynamic QR code generation in Bharat QR?
options: The payer need not enter the amount
The payer must enter the CVV
Payment is possible only in cash
explain: A dynamic QR already contains the amount, so the payer does not have to key it in.

q: The BHIM app is named after which personality?
explain: BHIM (Bharat Interface for Money) is named after B. R. Ambedkar.

q: On which date was BHIM launched?
explain: BHIM was launched on 30 December 2016 after the 2016 demonetisation.

q: How does BHIM differ from mobile wallets such as Paytm or MobiKwik?
options: BHIM stores money like a wallet
BHIM only moves money between bank accounts, whereas wallets hold money
explain: BHIM is only a mechanism to transfer money between bank accounts, while wallets keep a stored balance.

q: In BHIM, what does MMID stand for?
explain: MMID is the Mobile Money Identifier code that can be used to send money to non-UPI accounts.

q: In cheque truncation, what is sent to the drawee branch instead of the physical cheque?
options: An electronic image with MICR fields and other details
explain: The physical cheque is stopped en route and an electronic image goes ahead, cutting out paper movement.

q: Unlike RTGS, IMPS is available on which schedule?
options: 24x7 throughout the year including bank holidays
explain: IMPS is an instant service available round the clock including bank holidays.

q: NACH aims to integrate all regional versions of which service into one national system?
explain: NACH integrates regional ECS systems into one National Payment System and is claimed to be better than ECS.

q: NACH is designed for which type of transactions?
options: High-volume, low-value, repetitive and periodic ones
explain: NACH handles inter-bank high-volume, low-value payments that repeat at intervals.

q: Which NPCI network is the largest domestic ATM network in the country?
explain: The National Financial Switch (NFS) is the largest domestic ATM network.

q: Which of the following is NOT a service available on the NFS network?
explain: NFS offers cash withdrawal, balance enquiry, PIN change and mini statement, not loan sanction.

q: In NFS card-to-card fund transfer, which detail of the beneficiary must the remitter enter?
explain: Funds are transferred on the basis of the beneficiary's card number, entered by the remitter.

q: RuPay was conceived and launched by NPCI on which date?
explain: RuPay was launched on 26 March 2012.

q: With which networks does NPCI maintain ties to help RuPay gain international acceptance?
explain: The book names Discover Financial and JCB as RuPay's international acceptance partners.
